answer:
Quorum overlap is necessary, not sufficient. With R read responses and W write acknowledgements over N replicas, R + W > N guarantees only that the two sets intersect when membership is correct; Tycho states overlap "is necessary but not sufficient for freshness."

Four mechanisms explain a stale quorum read. (1) Acknowledgement scope: an acknowledged write means W voters accepted it, not that every replica applied it; async acknowledgement can reply before a standby catches up, and weak write concerns can roll back. (2) Version selection: the reader must pick the highest version among responses and repair lagging replicas; a selector that takes the first or fastest reply, ignores the newest replica, or cannot order concurrent versions serves old data. (3) Membership and sloppiness: sloppy quorum with hinted handoff stores writes on fallback nodes outside the strict preference list, and range movement can leave old and new quorums non-overlapping. (4) Read routing: follower reads are stale by default; linearizable reads need valid lease, read-index or quorum confirmation, and a leader that cannot confirm quorum must refuse.

Read repair and hinted handoff are "only best-effort"; convergence depends on anti-entropy. A highest-version selector, strict membership overlap and token- or lease-aware routing close these gaps. Evidence is documentary and synthetic, not production measurement.

evidence.claim: Quorum intersection is necessary but not sufficient for a fresh read; a read intersecting a write quorum can still be stale.
evidence.note: Observed: 'Overlap is necessary but not sufficient for freshness' and 'A read that intersects a write quorum can still return a stale value when the write failed, membership was sloppy, or the selector ignores the newest replica.'

evidence.claim: R + W > N makes read and write sets intersect, but the reader must select the highest version and repair stale replicas.
evidence.note: Observed: 'when R + W > N and membership is correctly configured, the sets intersect, but the reader must select the highest version and repair stale replicas'; also 'a read with too small R can return stale data'.

evidence.claim: Write acknowledgement is configured and staged: the client may be answered before a standby receives, flushes or applies the change.
evidence.note: Observed: synchronous replication distinguishes the stage at which a standby has written/flushed/applied changes; 'Async mode can reply before standby catches up.'

evidence.claim: Weaker write concern can roll back, so durability requires majority reads and writes; a replica count is not a durability guarantee.
evidence.note: Observed: '`{ w: 1 }` can roll back, so durability needs majority reads and writes'; token-less or rerouted reads may hit a replica lacking the session's data.

evidence.claim: Sloppy quorum sends requests to fallback nodes instead of enforcing strict membership; read repair and hinted handoff are best-effort.
evidence.note: Observed: 'Intersection alone does not guarantee freshness'; Dynamo/Riak sloppy quorum, hinted handoff and Merkle-tree anti-entropy are named as availability/recovery mechanisms, with Cassandra calling read repair and hinted handoff 'only best-effort'.

evidence.claim: Reads need a separately defined freshness policy: follower reads can be stale, and linearizable reads need lease, read-index or quorum confirmation.
evidence.note: Observed: 'local follower reads can be stale; linearizable reads require valid confirmation/lease/read-index semantics as implemented'; a leader that cannot confirm quorum must stop serving authoritative writes and linearizable reads.

evidence.claim: Clock-based last-write-wins ordering is not reliable evidence of recency or intent.
evidence.note: Observed: 'clock order is not evidence of user intent'; a clock adjustment must not accidentally make a future update permanently dominant; ties need a deterministic tie-breaker.

evidence.claim: Boundary: cross-region asynchronous replication can acknowledge a write in one region that is not yet visible in another.
evidence.note: Observed synthetic case staging 'a write acknowledged in A but not visible in B when the failover begins'; no production measurement is claimed.
